answer: Because ABS checks the bottom of the zone at both the middle and back edges, a pitch that lands in the lower‑tenth of the zone at the middle often falls outside the back‑edge limits and is ruled a ball. In 2025, 80 % (0.802) of low curveballs taken in that bottom tenth were called balls—much higher than fastballs (52 %) or sinkers (61 %). This two‑plane check makes low‑curveballs more likely to be called balls.
